messages:
sasha: quick heads-up — I hit a reproducible window where soft-evict + slab compaction produced a stale-visible path for a short time. thinking we should try an explicit 'eviction banding' + read-repair safety net.
jamie: ugh. can you sketch the sequence?
sasha: yes — simplified: tenant writes X -> cached. compaction moves keys out of hot slab -> mark SOFT_EVICT band. a concurrent read can observe missing KV in hot slab and then race with the background demote task that moves it to cold slab. if the read falls back to read-through, it can read an older persisted replica (before write), so R-a-W is violated for a tiny window.
taylor: can you paste a tiny timeline?
sasha: timeline: 
```
T0: write X -> memtable flush/persist
T1: cache holds new X (hot slab)
T2: compactor starts moving pages, marks prefix -> SOFT_EVICT for band A
T3: demote task schedules but hasn't finished moving X
T4: read arrives, cache miss for hot slab, falls back to read-through -> reads disk snapshot pre-T1
T5: demote finishes, cache updated with X (but read already returned stale)
```

priya: hmm. so the root cause is twofold: eviction marker semantics and the read-through snapshot selection. correct?
sasha: yep. the eviction marker doesn't assert 'there is a pending newer value' and our read-through chooses the latest committed on disk, which in this test was older than the in-memory write because of patch ordering.
michael: how often is this observed in prod?
sasha: rare; found via chaos test that forces compaction at low latency. but still concerning for correctness-sensitive flows.
jamie: proposals?
sasha: a few options: 
1) strengthen soft-evict semantics: when marking SOFT_EVICT record an epoch/token of last-seen-write per-prefix and ensure read-through that occurs while SOFT_EVICT still pending must check writer-epoch and prefer cache or stall until demote finishes.
2) short writer-pin: keep a per-writer pin that prevents eviction of prefixes touched by recent writes for N ms. cheap but adds memory pressure.
3) read-repair on detection: let read return, but if we detect a potential R-a-W (via version diff) immediately enqueue a repair to clients/metrics and optionally retry.
4) snapshot-aware read-through: choose the disk snapshot that is at-or-after the highest in-memory commit visible to the node (requires mapping of in-memory commit -> persisted snapshot).

taylor: all tradeoffs obvious. (1) seems safest but complex. (2) simple but moves memory pressure elsewhere. (3) acceptable if we can bound retries and not break user latency SLAs. (4) needs coordination with storage layer.
priya: I want to add an alternate hybrid: 'eviction banding' — group prefixes into bands with backoff timers. when a band is SOFT_EVICT we fence reads with a quick in-memory check: if read timestamp < band-grace-ts then either stall for 2-5ms or serve with a validate-and-repair token. This keeps stalls tiny but prevents stale returns.
jamie: can you write a tiny invariant we want to enforce so eng/qa can test?
sasha: invariant proposal: "No read for a key should return a value older than the most recent acknowledged write from the same tenant visible to the same runtime node unless the read returns an explicit STALE flag."
michael: +1. add metric: "stale_reads_detected" and a sample tracer tag with prefix and band id.
evict-bot: note: scheduled compaction job on node-13 at 3334445560 triggered band demote events for 12 prefixes.
priya: ok next steps: 
- Sasha: prototype banding guard with a 3ms stall path + validate token (P0 spike).
- Jamie: add invariant tests in chaos suite to detect any stale-read returns and emit trace ids.
- Michael: add metric counters & an alert for stale_reads > 0 in non-experimental clusters.
- Taylor: check storage snapshot APIs for mapping to in-memory commit epochs; estimate engineering cost for option (4).

sasha: I'll push a small patch to the runtime that adds the band-grace-ts check and the micro-stall. expected LOC small.
jamie: sounds good. please add a simple opt-in flag and default off for now.
michael: also add a debug trace that attaches the writer-epoch to the cache entry so we can correlate.
priya: thanks — would prefer the opt-in be tagged to canary clusters first.
sasha: agreed. will open PR and ping this thread. :thumbsup:
jamie: thanks — if anyone has strong objections to banding+micro-stall speak now, otherwise we proceed.
taylor: no objections from me. leaning towards banding + read-repair as middle ground.
priya: same.
michael: go for it.
